questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests must cover distributed transactions with asynchronous callbacks, idempotency keys to avoid duplicates across retries, and cross-region consistency. This mirrors real-world retail/back-office systems at Lyft/Goldman Sachs.

## Key Concepts
- Distributed async workflows
- Idempotency, exactly-once vs at-least-once
- Partial failure simulation (downstream outages)
- Data reconciliation and tombstones
- Latency budgets and observability (SLIs)

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo-idempotent processor
function processCheckoutEvent(event, store) {
  const key = event.idempotencyKey;
  if (store.has(key)) return store.get(key); // idempotent
  const res = doWork(event); // triggers downstream
  store.set(key, res);
  return res;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you structure a test to verify exactly-once semantics when events can be delivered multiple times?
- What metrics and dashboards would you use to detect latency regressions in the downstream flow during peak load?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests must validate correctness under concurrency, idempotency, and the coupling to an event bus, plus observable failure modes and retry behavior in production-like environments.

## Key Concepts
- Idempotency keys and idempotent operations
- Event-driven architecture and eventual consistency
- Concurrency and race conditions
- Fault injection and resilience testing

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-test sketch for idempotent create
const res1 = http.post('/orders', {customerId:'A', items:[1,2]}, {headers:{'Idempotency-Key':'k1'}});
const res2 = http.post('/orders', {customerId:'A', items:[1,2]}, {headers:{'Idempotency-Key':'k1'}});
assert(res1.body.id === res2.body.id && res1.status===201 && res2.status===201);
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate idempotency across multiple data centers?
- How would you simulate partial event-bus outages without affecting real data?
